blocks.value: Knitwear Design courses deal with wools, yarns and other materials required to make the final knitted apparel. Under these courses, students learn about technology, manufacturing, stitching, pattern-making, trend analysis, forecasting, sketching of cloth, production of cloth , etc.

Knitwear Design programs are offered at various levels including UG, PG, Diploma, and Certification . Some popular courses under this specialisation include BDes in Knitwear Design, MDes in Knitwear Design, Diploma in Knitwear Designing, Certificate in Knitwear Designing , etc.

Admission to Knitwear Design courses is majorly based on the merit system, however, NIFTs in India conduct their NIFT entrance exams for candidates. Interested candidates can continue reading the article for more Knitwear Design course details.

faqs.question: What is Knitwear Design?
faqs.answer: A Knitwear Design course includes the study of wools, yarns and other materials required to create finished knitted clothing. They get knowledge on how to employ machinery, tools and technology to create certain designs and outfits. The Knitwear Design course places a strong emphasis on acquiring skills and knowledge in pattern creativity, knitting and sewing, creating full-length clothing and mediating clothing styles. Knitwear designers play an important part in developing the newest trends and adjusting to changing consumer tastes in the fashion industry, which is always changing.

faqs.question: What is the duration of BDes in Knitwear Design?
faqs.answer: The Bachelor of Design in Knitwear Design is a three-year undergraduate programme. The course's overarching goal is to produce professionals who can comprehend and apply the complexities and technicalities of knitwear design, production, quality control, promotion, branding, and management. Students must have passed Class 12 with at least 50% marks from a recognised board in order to be eligible for BDes Knitwear Design. Admission to this degree will be granted based on the candidate's performance in the Class 12 test or their success in the entrance exams administered by admission authorities. Check BDes Course Details

faqs.question: What are the latest trends in Knitwear Design field?
faqs.answer: With new scientific inventions, changes and advancements in every industry are being witnessed. Likewise, development in the fashion industry is also being experienced and will continue to grow over time. New kinds of fibres are being produced, and methods to weave and knit are also evolving. Such emerging techniques and products will keep sprouting from efficient yard spinners and fibre producers, making sure that there is constant progress,  improvement and not a moment of stagnation from their side. Some of the latest and upcoming designing techniques are mentioned below: Smart textiles where generally fabric is categorized into five kinds, based on their component fibre. These organic fabrics are silk, wool, linen, cotton and synthetic and inorganic fibre are gold, glass and asbestos. Smart textiles are so-called, as they can detect and respond to spurs from the surrounding nature, which can be biological chemical mechanical or any other type of environment. Soon Knitwear designers are about to work with such textiles and bring a change in the fashion industry. 3D Knitwear designing is what is coming next in this field. One can customize styles according to his/ her comfort. 3D Knitwear seems effortless and has a better finish than handcrafted sewed ones. With ecological and environmental issues on the rise, 3D knitting will be a new and fresh approach to reduce it. It will help with sustainable fashion for people because it will help in cost and time, higher productivity, more energy efficiency, and waste reduction. Shapewear & seamless garments on customized knitting. This makes attires with the application of circular knitting machines which make the entire clothing with the help of automated computers which has many directions for stitching patterns. And body-mapped.

faqs.question: What are the job profiles at which Knitwear Design graduates can work?
faqs.answer: The designing graduates in Knitwear design can join the industry at the below-mentioned job positions: Knitwear Designer – The knitwear designer is a specialist involved with the ideation of designs, and patterns and also with manufacturing knitted apparel and accessories. The designers are involved in large-scale as well as exclusive knitwear manufacturing. Moreover, some of the popular designer work as stylists and pattern makers to supply hand sketching or CAD for the production of knitwear. Fashion Forecasters – The fashion industry is ever-changing, every day a new trend is set, therefore, as fashion forecasters, they are required to research and analyse the worldwide fashion industry. The fashion forecasters work with fashion designers to help them develop new trends for the market, Quality controllers for fabric – The quality controllers are involved in setting standards for the fabric to differentiate original and quality products from faux material. They are responsible for maintaining a differentiation in the quality of original fabrics from synthetic ones and also making the consumer aware of it. Some manufacturers adopt unethical practices of selling faux material as the original at a high cost. Therefore, it is the job of Quality Controllers to stop such unethical practices. Product Research Specialist – As a research specialist for knitwear products, one can develop new techniques for product development, quality improvement, and fabric colour enhancement methods. This research help in market research and analysing trends for knitwear products. Product research specialist is highly demanded professionals in the Fashion and Design Industry for their experience and knowledge of market research which is helpful in New Product Development as well as Product Innovation.

faqs.question: How does the job profile of a Knitwear Designer differ from that of a Fashion Designer?
faqs.answer: Fashion design is a form of art dedicated to the creation of clothing and other lifestyle accessories. Modern fashion design is divided into two basic categories: haute couture and ready-to-wear. Fashion design is influenced by cultural and social latitudes, and has varied over time and place. Fashion designers attempt to design clothes which are functional as well as aesthetically pleasing. They consider who is likely to wear a garment and the situations in which it will be worn. They have a wide range and combinations of materials to work with and a wide range of colors, patterns and styles to choose from. The Knitwear Design specialization offered in Fashion & Textiles has been introduced keeping in view the future requirements of the Indian knitting industry This involves creation of original fabric designs. Knitwear teaches the skills and construction techniques in order to produce quality knitwear designs.Majorly this involves production/design of winter wear. Hope this information helps. faqs.question: What is the scope of Knitwear Design in India and abroad?
faqs.answer: The Knitwear industry is composed of a promising future, reinforced with new-age technology, talented Knitwear designers and lots of creativity. Students belonging to this domain have a wide range of career opportunities in Textile and Knit industry, handloom and handicrafts organizations, NGOs, design studios, export houses and mills. With the boom in online shopping, the scope for designers is only opening more opportunities as buyers and sellers and merchandisers. During the 4 years of graduation, students are exposed to the education and talent of professional designers and teachers. They learn and enhance their creative vision, technical skills with flat knits, circular knits and computerized knitting. They acquire the wisdom to work for all categories of Knitwear apparel be it, menswear, women's wear, kids wear, sportswear,  leisurewear, winter wear and intimate wear. They grasp the knowledge of what and which resource is required to knit a fine garment as per needed by the client. The placements at fashion schools are mostly done in private companies, MNCs and startups.
